rows.agency_label: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget
rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: BKCB2 requests a baselined annual budget increase of $26,160 to send an annual direct mailer to the ~80,000 households in BKCD2 to inform them of the City Charter-mandated municipal information, resident assistance, and civic participation opportunities available to them through their Community Board and District Office. Printing: $0.08/postcard = $6,400 USPS EDDM bulk postage: $0.247/postcard = $19,760 Investing in Community Boards is an investment in accountable, equitable, and responsive government for every New Yorker. Community Boards play a uniquely democratic role in shaping development, addressing neighborhood concerns, ensuring residents have a voice in city decisions, and educating residents about municipal systems and functions. Yet we operate with one third of the staff of City Council offices despite serving a similar-sized population, and are typically allocated an OTPS budget of less than $15k per year. Increasing our baseline budget specifically for outreach purposes would strengthen our ability to reach and engage the public, conduct meaningful planning, and respond effectively to community needs. Outreach will become even more urgent in the coming decade as Community Board term limits take effect, thereby decreasing institutional knowledge and increasing the need for new Member recruitment.
